messages.author: 2a4b4922857caa2c
messages.subject: ggplot2 stat_density problem
parts:
Dear all,

I am experiencing a problem with stat_density in ggplot2 0.9.0. It
seems that the new implementation of the function cuts a lot of data,
thus producing crippled results.

This is what I used to get with an earlier version (don't remember
which one) of ggplot2:

http://dl.dropbox.com/u/18999200/Fig13_then.png

This is what I get now:

http://dl.dropbox.com/u/18999200/Fig13_now.png

And this is the code that I am using:

trace.data <- make.groups("Arrivals from transactional
data"=historical_interarrival_times,
"Synthetically generated
arrivals"=simulated_interarrival_times)
png("Fig13.png")
ggplot(trace.data, aes(x=data)) + geom_density() + facet_grid(. ~
which) +
scale_x_log10("Interarrival Times (seconds)",
limits=c(0.1,2E6)) +
scale_y_continuous("Density")
dev.off()


I am running R version 2.15.0.

Could you please help me to fix this problem?

Thank you very much in advance.


Best regards,
Mauro Tortonesi

--

There's an ugly bug with facet_grid in 0.9.0 where it would drop duplicate data. It's fixed in the development version, which you can install with the instructions here:
https://github.com/wch/ggplot2/wiki/Installing-the-development-version-of-ggplot2


-Winston

> A quick follow up. Oddly enough, this problem seems to happen only if
> I use facet_grid.

Actually not that odd. There is (was) a bug in facet_grid. See
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/443 . It will be fixed in the
next release of ggplot2 (version 0.9.1). As a workaround until then, you
can add a unique dummy variable to trace.data.

trace.data$dummy <- seq(length=nrow(trace.data))
